data.analysis: Choose N=3: the main opportunities are distinct ways to improve the Y stencil’s memory access and reuse, and the roughly 30-minute remaining window favors three focused, concurrent investigations over redundant topics. The supplied baseline is valid and correct on the stated GH200/CUDA 12.6.3 target; its three measured times average 3.5815 µs (score 0.5). In the supplied launch, each block has only four adjacent X threads while Y spans 64, and the kernel uses shared memory and two barriers. This suggests testing better warp-level coalescing and alternative reuse, but the tiny fixed workload may also be launch-bound; no gain is assumed. Preserve the period-63 endpoint convention, coefficients, full output, signed-input correctness, and oracle tolerance. Measure with the official full-run protocol and compare candidates only after correctness checks; require independent confirmation for final G. CUDA’s 12.6.3 Best Practices Guide explains the 32-byte transaction rationale for coalesced accesses: https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/12.6.3/cuda-c-best-practices-guide/index.html (section 9.2.1).

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single direct-global-load kernel with one output per thread and no shared memory or per-thread multi-output reuse. Map each warp to adjacent X outputs at a fixed Y and Z, then compare suitable block/grid mappings and boundary-index handling. Compute all eight Y neighbors with the supplied coefficients and period-63 endpoint convention; produce every output without modifying inputs or relying on scratch contents. Validate signed varying inputs against the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
children.subject: Coalesced direct-global one-output-per-thread kernel

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single shared-memory tiled kernel that loads Y neighborhoods cooperatively with contiguous X lanes and reuses the tile across multiple Y outputs. Explore tile heights and launch shapes while ensuring every required halo is initialized and periodic wrapping uses period 63, including the endpoints. Preserve the exact stencil, full output, input buffers, and scratch rules. Validate against the oracle on signed varying inputs, then compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
children.subject: Coalesced shared-memory Y tiles with explicit periodic halos

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, investigate a single kernel where each thread handles several consecutive Y outputs using a register rolling window, with warp lanes still accessing adjacent X values. Explore small output-chunk sizes to balance neighbor reuse against register pressure and occupancy. Do not use shared memory or extra launches in this track. Handle period-63 wrapping exactly at tile and domain boundaries, compute every output for varying signed inputs, and preserve the supplied tolerance and buffer constraints. Validate with the oracle and compare repeated official full-run timings with the baseline.
children.subject: Register rolling-window multi-output-per-thread kernel
